scope: Independent retained complete assembly/pseudocode and exact new production-source review for three normal pool-clear byte-state projections and three existing-provider source bindings. No original-file reads, original execution or reviewer tests.
findings: Raw DWORD count at pool+64 controls nonzero loop entry, including negative signed representations; zero skips array access but still performs final resets.

Each entered iteration rereads old count, retains its signed64 index, stores wrapping DWORD old-1 before loading live array data at pool+8, then reads block at data+old_index*8-8 with modulo64 arithmetic.
The lower pointer-only free receives the loaded block. The subsequent condition reads live count again; mutations to count, array data or entries remain observable on later iterations.
Three final QWORD zero stores occur at pool+68,+70,+78 in exact order and access width; no extra count write, separate DWORD resets or rollback is added.
Vptr, array data/capacity, inline/stale entries and unrelated bytes are not cleared by the source helper itself; no pointer-array free, constructor or pool-destructor effect is invented.
Caller EDX4080/4056/4032 values are retained as static facts in target order002d70/002dc0/002e10; the existing pointer-only free boundary does not claim sized-free or register ABI equivalence.
RecoveredPoolClearEffects preserves inherited document/node-clear source bindings and closes exactly three existing NativeDocumentEffects pool-clear providers on shared bounded memory.

Each target has one normal wrapper plus one numeric-tagged final source bridge; two tagged definitions do not imply two native functions. The N19 append binding and separate N18 allocation adapter are not changed.
limitations: Bounded byte-state normal projection only; native fault, register ABI, unwind/EH and concurrency equivalence remain unproven.
Free04b0f8 remains a mandatory lower provider; no heap/CRT body or native allocator ownership implementation is recovered.
Pool destructors001bb0/001c30/001cb0/001d30 and full lifecycle, node virtual/parser/DOM materialization remain open.
Missing or ambiguous memory mappings produce source-interface exceptions rather than native fault equivalence; fixture effects and constructed tests are not original execution proof.
